steps.say: Each turn starts with an opening card. You and SAE each pick one in secret, then both are shown together. An opening card is used only for its event: its action points are not spent. Pick Maastricht Treaty.

SAE picked Handover of Hong Kong. The card with more action points goes first: Hong Kong has 4 and Maastricht 2, so SAE's event happens first. On a tie, LIO's pick would go first, whichever side's card it is.

Maastricht gives you {eventPoints:e1-lio-001} point now. You can place where you already have influence ({influenceIn:lio}), next to it, or next to the United States ({homeNeighbours:lio}). For the rest of this turn, each time you spend points, you spend 1 more.

variants.say: Maastricht gives you {eventPoints:e1-lio-001} point now. You can place next to the United States ({homeNeighbours:lio}). For the rest of this turn, each time you spend points, you spend 1 more.

steps.say: Now the card plays: LIO, SAE, LIO, SAE. Play NATO Enlargement 1999 for its points: 3, plus 1 from Maastricht, so {cardPoints:e1-lio-004} to spend. All of a play's points go to one action.

You control a country when your influence there is at least its stability, and at least SAE's influence plus its stability. Mexico has stability 2: 2 influence controls it. Placing in a country SAE controls costs 2 points for each influence. Where you can place is fixed when the play starts.
Primakov's U-turn is SAE's card. You can play it only for its points, and its event still happens, as SAE's event.

You choose whether the event comes before or after you spend. It makes you spend 1 fewer for the rest of the turn. Before: 1, plus 1 from Maastricht, minus 1, gives {pointsBefore:e1-sae-008} point. After: you spend {pointsAfter:e1-sae-008}, and the penalty only reaches spends later this turn, when you have no plays left. Chapter 6 shows the one exception: points spent on the tech race cancel the event.

variants.say: You choose whether the event comes before or after you spend. It makes you spend 1 fewer for the rest of the turn. Before: 1, plus 1 from Maastricht, minus 1, minus {modifierTakesOff:e1-neu-001} from Rwandan Genocide, and never below 1, gives {pointsBefore:e1-sae-008} point. After: you also spend {pointsAfter:e1-sae-008}, so here the order doesn't change your points, and the penalty only reaches spends later this turn, when you have no plays left. Chapter 6 shows the one exception: points spent on the tech race cancel the event.

steps.say: Turn 2: both hands fill back up to 8. Pick Partnership for Peace, and keep Desert Storm Coalition, Budapest Memorandum and Second Chechen War for the next chapters.
Play Desert Storm Coalition for its {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points and intervene in any country where SAE has influence. It doesn't need to be next to yours.

There are no dice: you draw a card numbered 1 to 6 from your Contingency deck. Result = draw + points spent - 2 x the country's stability. If the result is above 0, SAE loses that much influence there, and what is left over becomes yours. With {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points, a stability-2 country such as Crimea gives a result equal to your draw. An intervention in a battleground raises Escalation by 1.

With {cardPoints:e1-lio-006} points, a stability-2 country such as Crimea gives a result {belowDraw:e1-lio-006} below your draw. An intervention in a battleground raises Escalation by 1.

steps.say: Both sides see every draw. A used card stays out until the deck is reshuffled, when two are left, so a low draw now means higher ones are still to come.
